headline_marked: [[Dumpster diver builds Proxmox server]] from weekly landfill runs for SSDs, HDDs, GPUs, and RAM
headline: Dumpster diver builds Proxmox server from weekly landfill runs for SSDs, HDDs, GPUs, and RAM
summary: A tech enthusiast regularly salvages valuable PC components and even an Asus ROG laptop from e-waste, using them to build a powerful home lab server.
details: A tech enthusiast has successfully built a home lab-worthy Proxmox server using PC parts scavenged from a county landfill. This individual, known as Tsuto on Reddit, now conducts weekly raids on the dump's electronics recycling area.

Their finds include valuable components such as SSDs, HDDs, GPUs, and RAM, along with complete laptops. Tsuto notes that while many parts are older, they are still sought after given current component shortages.

One notable find was an Asus ROG laptop, which only required a $25 battery. This laptop, featuring an Intel Core i7-4710HQ, 16GB RAM, and a GeForce GTX 860M, is now used for casual gaming by their son.

The Proxmox server itself is configured with two mirrored 256GB SSDs for the OS, an additional 1TB SSD for fast storage, and three 2TB HDDs in RAID1 for ZFS storage. Despite the numerous salvaged parts, Tsuto did purchase a Core i7-7700 and 64GB of RAM to finalize the system.
The article also highlights that such scavenging is not universally possible, with many recycling centers having security and cameras to prevent unauthorized removal of electronics.
